The worker complained of continuing pain and visions involving her family in dangerous situations.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [3 pages]
The worker's request to reconsider Decision No. 71/91 was denied.  [3 pages]

DecKeywords: Access to worker file, statutory; Medical examination (employer request); Procedure (medical examination) (employer request) (access to worker file)
DecSummary: The worker applied for an order that he not be required to attend a medical examination.  The employer previously requested that the worker attend an examination.  In Decision No. 1004/89, the Tribunal decided that the worker did not have to attend for that examination since the employer had not applied for access to the worker's file.  However, the employer could not have known of Decision No. 1004/89 since it was released after the hearing of this application.

The worker was receiving a provisional pension for non-organic disability.  He was appealing denial of a pension for organic disability.  The Panel wanted to proceed using the whole person approach.  As a Board reassessment of the non-organic disability was imminent, the hearing was adjourned.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Aggravation (preexisting condition) (disc, degeneration); Continuing entitlement; Medical report (clinical notes)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury in July 1980.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying ongoing benefits subsequent to April 1991.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF}; Continuing entitlement
DecSummary: The worker suffered a minor low back strain in June 1984.  The employer appealed granting of temporary benefits from May 1985 to August 1987 and granting of a 15% pension.

The worker suffered a compensable injury in 1978.  In 1984, he began a formal training programme sponsored by the Board.  Until 1988, he completed most of his courses.  In the winter of 1988 and in the 1988/89 academic year, he had to drop out of the programme due to psychological difficulties.  However, he managed to complete a substantial number of courses in the summer of 1989.  The Board refused to continue sponsoring the worker in September 1989. The worker returned to school without the sponsorship but was unable to complete any courses.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer refusing to continue sponsorship.

A courier suffered a back injury in August 1987 and received benefits for 10 days.  In 1988, he began work as a rehabilitation counsellor.  In 1989, the worker began to experience back problems.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for his back condition in 1989.
The worker's application for leave to appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue the issue of chronic pain at the Board.  [3 pages]

A construction labourer fell about four feet in July 1986.  He did not lose any time from work until October 1986.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement to benefits for a back disability.

The worker was appealing a 1986 Hearings Officer decision which denied continuation of vocational rehabilitation services that had been discontinued in 1983.  The Board had determined, in 1983, that the worker was not co-operating and that he would not benefit from the services.  The worker claimed that he had not received the proper amount of benefits during the period that he was attending a training course in 1983 and that this contributed to the discontinuance of training.

The worker suffered a severe head injury in 1962 in a compensable accident when a ceiling collapsed.  The worker received a provisional pension for psychiatric disability until 1986.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying psychiatric benefits subsequent to 1986.

DecKeywords: Consequences of injury (residual weakness); Subsequent incidents (outside work)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a left knee sprain in October 1982.  The worker's doctor suspected a torn meniscus and recommended surgery.  However, the worker was reluctant to undergo surgery.  The doctor authorized physiotherapy and suggested that the worker wear a hinged knee corset.  In January 1983, the worker slipped and fell in an icy parking lot and suffered a fractured left knee.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the fracture.

DecKeywords: Employer (successor rights); Notice of hearing; Parties (interest of employer); Parties (of record); Parties (representation) (authority); Standing; Withdrawal (of appeal)
DecSummary: In June 1991, the employer filed an appeal from a decision granting benefits to the worker.  In September 1991, the hearing was adjourned.  In December 1991, the employer's account was closed by the Board with the notation 'unable to locate'.  In April 1992, the hearing commenced with the presentation of evidence for one day.  In June 1992, the employer ceased to exist.  In July 1992, the hearing continued for another day.  In August 1992, the Panel was advised that the employer ceased to exist by an employee of the employer who had been representing the employer.

The worker fell at work in May 1974.  He received benefits until July 1974 for a hand and low back condition.  There were no further back complaints until December 1974, when the worker was admitted to hospital after falling down some stairs.  The next medical reference to back pain was in April 1985.

The request of the worker's widow to reconsider Decision No. 697/91 was denied.  In Decision No. 697/91, the original hearing panel found that the worker was entitled to a pension for silicosis but denied dependency benefits subsequent to his death.  The widow did not raise any new arguments that had not been considered at the original hearing.  The hearing panel had sufficient evidence to reach its conclusion.  [6 pages]

The worker suffered a low back injury in July 1956 and received benefits until May 1957.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further benefits including benefits for back surgery in 1973 and 1978.
The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying commutation of the worker's pension, valued at about $80,000.  He wanted the commutation for the purpose of debt liquidation.

DecKeywords: Bronchitis; Chronic obstructive lung disease; Exposure (silica dust); Heart attack; Mining (gold)
DecSummary: The worker was a gold miner from 1937 to 1969.  He died as a result of a heart attack in 1987.  The worker's widow appealed decisions of the Board denying the worker entitlement for chronic obstructive lung disease (COLD) and denying dependency benefits for the worker's death.
The appeal was withdrawn to allow the worker to pursue the issue of chronic pain at the Board.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Pensions (AMA Guides) (respiratory impairment); Pensions (assessment) (respiratory impairment); Pensions (assessment) (silicosis); Preexisting condition (silicosis); Pulmonary embolism
DecSummary: The worker retired at age 65 in 1976.  He was granted a 30% pension for silicosis in 1983, retroactive to 1977.  In 1984 the pension was increased to 40%.  The worker's health deteriorated in 1985 and he died in June 1985.  The worker's widow appealed a decision denying her dependency benefits.  To succeed on the appeal, the widow would have to show either that silicosis was a significant factor in the worker's death, or that, at the time of his death, the worker was 100% disabled by silicosis.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (consideration of evidence); Scope of hearing (where leave granted)
DecSummary: The worker applied for leave to appeal a decision of the Appeal Board denying entitlement to benefits in 1953 and 1954 and denying benefits subsequent to 1972.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for hearing loss.  On the evidence, the Panel found that the worker was suffering primarily from conductive hearing loss caused by scarring and retraction of the tympanic membrane and cholosteatoma, which are symptoms of otitis media.  The worker's hearing loss was not the sensorineural hearing loss that can related to noise exposure.
The hearing was adjourned to allow the worker to obtain a representative.  The worker had not fully understood the implications of proceeding unrepresented.  [3 pages]

The worker suffered a jerking injury to his left elbow.  The Board granted benefits for epicondylitis.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for left ulnar neuropathy, which the worker claimed was also caused by the compensable accident.
The employer failed to give the required notice that it would be relying on a transcript of evidence taken before the Appeal Board, particularly the evidence of the worker's treating physician.
The worker suffered a compensable injury in August 1986.  He appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting only 50% temporary partial disability benefits subsequent to September 1986.

A bricklayer was appealing the earnings basis for calculation of his pension.  The Panel noted a number of decisions regarding seasonal work and unemployment insurance benefits and granted an adjournment to allow the worker to consider whether to proceed with the appeal.  [4 pages]

The worker's request to reconsider Decision No. 520/91 was denied.  The original hearing panel considered the evidence and arrived at a conclusion regarding the amount of the worker's compensable hearing loss.  The worker did not raise any new arguments on this application.  [5 pages]

DecKeywords: Pensions (lump sum) (ten per cent pension) (advantage to worker)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying commutation of her 8% pension.  It had not been shown that payment of the pension in a lump sum would not be to the advantage of the worker within s. 45(4).  Previous Tribunal decisions indicated that if there were strong indications that the worker's condition was likely to deteriorate, it may not be to the worker's advantage to commute the pension.  In this case, medical evidence from a Board doctor indicated only that it was possible that the worker's condition could deteriorate.  The appeal was allowed.  [5 pages]

DecKeywords: Suitable employment; Availability for employment (relocation); Board Directives and Guidelines (retroactivity); Board Directives and Guidelines (supplements, temporary) (policy change); Pensions (assessment) (eye) (enucleation); Pensions (assessment) (eye) (ophthalmalia); Rehabilitation, vocational (cooperation); Supplements, older worker; Supplements, temporary
DecSummary: The worker was involved in an accident in December 1973 that led to the surgical removal (enucleation) of his left eye in June 1974.  At the time of the accident the worker was aged 44 and his employment to that time consisted of operating heavy machinery, such as bulldozers, in mining and logging operations.  He had a grade six education in the French language only.  The worker was awarded an 18% pension, but was denied a temporary supplement.  He appealed the level of his pension and the denial of the temporary supplement.

The worker suffered a left knee injury in February 1986.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits from September 1988 to March 1989.  On the evidence, the worker refused suitable light work at no wage loss which could be done either sitting or standing and which was within the worker's medical restrictions.  The appeal was dismissed.  [5 pages]

On May 14, 1986, the worker struck the left side of his head on a drum.  Two days later, he suffered a cerebral infarction.  The Board granted benefits for head injuries but denied entitlement for the stroke.  The worker appealed denial of benefits for the stroke.

DecKeywords: Benefit of the doubt; Chronic pain; Disablement (nature of work); Psychotraumatic disability; Transcript
DecSummary: In a preliminary matter, the Panel accepted into evidence portions of the transcript of the testimony of the worker and the employer's human resources manager before the Hearings Officer.  It was not necessary to re-question the worker as the same representatives for both parties were present before the Hearings Officer and had been given full rights to question and cross-question the witnesses at that time.   The employer now had a different human resources manager, so the evidence before the Hearings Officer was the best evidence that could be received.

The worker suffered a crush injury to his hand in 1983, for which he was awarded a 3% pension.  The worker appealed decisions of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain and denying an increase in the pension.

The worker was appealing a decision denying continuing entitlement for a left knee injury related to an accident in 1980.  There was a prior compensable left knee injury in 1969 which the Board had not considered in relation to this claim.  The Panel declined jurisdiction and sent the matter back to the Board.  [3 pages]

The worker was appealing denial of continuing benefits.  A pre-hearing medical report obtained by the Tribunal Counsel Office recommended a psychiatric assessment.  The worker agreed to such an assessment but a report could not be obtained before the hearing.  The hearing was adjourned to obtain a psychiatric assessment and to obtain material from the Board regarding its investigations or any chronic pain or psychotraumatic disability.

The Panel clarified Decision No. 587/91 regarding the status of a defendant in a civil case who did not attend the hearing of a s. 17 application.  That defendant was the Schedule 1 employer of the plaintiff.  Accordingly, the right of action against that defendant was taken away.  [6 pages]

DecKeywords: Consequences of injury (iatrogenic illness) (treatment) (investigative procedures); Evidence (epidemiological); Firefighter; Industrial Disease Standards Panel (heart disease) (firefighter)
DecSummary: A firefighter suffered a syncope attack (transient loss of consciousness due to inadequate blood flow to the brain) while fighting a fire in November 1987.  He returned to modified work in December 1987.  The worker was off work again in February and March 1988 for further testing.  As a result of this testing, the worker underwent a bypass in July 1988.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for the testing and the bypass surgery.

DecKeywords: Availability for employment (refusing suitable work); Available employment (offer from accident employer)
DecSummary: A construction labourer suffered a severe hand injury in November 1985, when he was 61 years old.  In October 1987, he was awarded a 17.2% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits from June 1987 to October 1987 and denying an older worker supplement subsequent to October 1987.

Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer, except for documents which were not used by the Board in making the decision under appeal.  The file contained some reports subsequent to the reports which were used by the Board and those reports should be withheld.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Aggravation (compensable injury); Suitable employment; Chronic pain; Maximal medical rehabilitation
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back strain in July 1985 while carrying a carton weighing about 20 pounds.  She made a number of unsuccessful returns to work.  In July 1987, she returned to work for five days but stopped due to back pain.  She was awarded a 15% pension for organic back disability.  Later, this award was replaced by a 20% pension for chronic pain.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits subsequent to July 1987.

DecKeywords: Evidence (hearsay); Procedure (reconsideration) (constitution of Panel); Procedure (reconsideration) (multiple applications); Reconsideration (new evidence)
DecSummary: In Decision No. 762/91, the hearing panel found that the worker was suffering from chronic pain rather than fibromyalgia during a period in 1985 and 1986.  The worker applied for reconsideration.  In Decisions No. 762/91RI and 762/91R2, the original hearing panel found that criteria for reopening the decision had not been met with regard to the finding on chronic pain.  The worker now made a second application to reconsider Decision No. 762/91 as well as an application to reconsider Decisions No. 762/91RI and 762/91R2.

DecKeywords: Access to worker file, statutory (harmful information)
DecSummary: The employer appealed a decision denying access to certain medical documents.  These documents had been withheld from the worker under s. 77(2) since they contained information which was potentially harmful to the worker.

The worker suffered a shoulder injury for which he was awarded a pension.  He returned to work for a number of years until his employment was terminated in July 1988.  In 1989 The Hearings Officer granted a temporary supplement from November 1989.  The worker appealed denial of a supplement from July 1988.

The employer applied for an order requiring the worker to attend a medical examination.  The employer's compensation goals related to initial and continuing entitlement and SIEF relief.  The examination was important to achieving those goals since the reports on file did not address in any detail the questions of level of disability, ability to perform modified work or preexisting conditions.  The application was allowed.  [6 pages]

DecKeywords: Arising out of employment (reasonably incidental activity test); Board Directives and Guidelines (in the course of employment) (personal activity); In the course of employment (reasonably incidental activity test) (personal needs); Presumptions (entitlement)
DecSummary: The worker arrived at work prior to the start of her shift.  She went to the washroom before starting to work.  While reaching back to grab a flap of material so that she could do up a button on her jump suit, she felt pain in her back.  The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting entitlement.

DecKeywords: Apportionment (pensions); Board Directives and Guidelines (second accident); Chronic pain; Consequences of injury (iatrogenic illness) (treatment) (surgery); Depression; Psychotraumatic disability; Obesity; Recurrences (compensable injury) (strains and sprains)
DecSummary: The worker sustained an acute contusion and sprain of her back in a compensable accident when she fell down stairs in February 1988.  In January 1989 the worker was delivered of a still-born child which caused severe depression.  The worker received temporary benefits until August 1989 and returned to work from September to December 1989.  In November 1989 she was diagnosed with diabetes.  The worker's overweight condition developed into gross obesity.  She gave birth to a healthy baby in June 1990.

The hearing was adjourned to allow the worker to obtain medical reports from several psychiatrists who had examined the worker.  It would be necessary to consider these reports before reaching a conclusion.  It made sense to obtain them before the hearing rather than requesting them post-hearing.  [3 pages]

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (evidence to support Appeal Board conclusion)
DecSummary: The worker applied for leave to appeal a decision of the Appeal Board denying entitlement for tinnitus and loss of balance associated with hearing loss.  New medical reports submitted by the worker were not substantially different from reports which were before the Board.  There was evidence to support the Appeal Board conclusion that the worker's ear complaints were not caused by employment.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a back injury.  The worker did not lose time from work immediately.  There was some seemingly conflicting evidence from a co-worker.  However, a close examination of the co-worker's evidence showed that it could be reconciled with the evidence of the worker.  It was also understandable that three months later, while seeking treatment at a hospital, the worker could not remember the exact date of the accident.  The appeal was allowed.  [6 pages]

DecKeywords: Consequences of injury (altered gait); Continuity (of treatment)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a right knee injury in December 1969 and received benefits until September 1970.  He suffered a left knee injury in February 1981 for which he was awarded a 5% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Appeals Adjudicator denying further benefits for the right knee.

DecKeywords: Aggravation (preexisting condition) (osteoarthritis) (hip); Climate (cold); Disablement (repetitive work); Disablement (working conditions) (cold); Significant contribution (of employment to disability)
DecSummary: The worker was a meat wrapper from 1981 to 1987.  She worked in a refrigerated room.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for osteoarthritis of the right hip.
The worker claimed to have injured her elbow at work by bumping it on the corner of a wooden table.

DecKeywords: Disablement (nature of work); Medical report (certainty of diagnosis)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Appeal Board denying entitlement for shoulder, arm, neck and low back problems which the worker related to the nature of her employment.  The worker's job involved considerable bending, twisting and lifting.  Although there was no change in the worker's job that brought on the condition and no definitive diagnosis of the condition, the Panel found that work was a significant contributing factor.  The appeal was allowed.  [10 pages]

DecKeywords: Post-traumatic stress disorder; Psychotraumatic disability; Police; Subsequent incidents (outside work)
DecSummary: The worker was a police officer.  On August 10, 1984, the worker and his partner were called to a hospital where a prisoner was being treated.  A scuffle broke out during which the prisoner grabbed the worker's gun.  The worker's staff sergeant, who was also there to assist the other officers, was shot in the leg.  The worker suffered a back injury during the scuffle for which he was awarded a 5% pension.

DecKeywords: Independent operator; Evidence (confidential information) (assessment files); Procedure (disclosure of evidence)
DecSummary: The claimant was an expert on hovercrafts.  He was retained by O Co. for two days in January 1986 to modify its hovercraft.  He was subsequently hired on an intermittent basis to demonstrate hovercrafts for O Co., which was a distributor of hovercrafts.  The claimant was injured while performing such a demonstration.  The issue was whether the claimant was a worker of O Co. or an independent operator.

The worker suffered a knee injury in 1961 for which he was awarded a 5% pension, increased to 8% in 1988.  He also suffered a low back injury in 1964 for which he was awarded a 15% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying an increase in the pensions.

The worker's application to reconsider Decision No. 33/91 was denied.  In Decision No. 33/91, the hearing panel denied temporary partial benefits for two weeks in October 1988.  The worker submitted 19 grounds for his application to reconsider.  The grounds dealt with minor discrepancies in the hearing panel's description of the evidence and with the worker's reasons for questioning the hearing panel's conclusions.  None of the submissions satisfied the Panel that there were grounds to reconsider.  [10 pages]

DecKeywords: Epilepsy; Medical opinion (seizures); Temporary partial disability
DecSummary: The worker fell in January 1983, injuring his low back, neck and head.  He received benefits for a number of periods including the period from October 1986 to July 1989 when he received 50% temporary partial disability benefits.  In July 1989, he was awarded a 20% pension for chronic pain.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer finding that the worker was entitled to 50% benefits, rather than 100% benefits, from October 1986 to July 1989.

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (consideration of evidence); Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (consideration of issue)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a fracture of the left patella during a compensable accident in July 1974.  In December 1974 idiopathic avascular necrosis of the head of the right femur was diagnosed and a hip replacement was required in June 1975.  The worker sought leave to appeal a decision of the Appeal Board denying entitlement for the right hip condition.

DecKeywords: Benefit of the doubt; Board Directives and Guidelines (hearing loss); Hearing loss
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision denying him a pension for hearing loss.  The worker met the requirement of five years' exposure to hazardous levels of industrial noise.  However, Board policy also requires a hearing loss of at least 35 decibels in one ear and at least 25 decibels in the other.

DecKeywords: Availability for employment (incarceration); Available employment (offer from accident employer); Incarceration; Rehabilitation, vocational (availability) (incarceration); Rehabilitation, vocational (cooperation); Temporary partial disability (level of benefits) (retroactive adjudication)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a back injury in 1981.  The Board denied benefits while the worker was incarcerated in Alberta from November 1982 to August 1986.  In August 1986, benefits were reinstituted.  The worker was awarded a 30% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits while the worker was incarcerated.

DecKeywords: Benefit of the doubt; Disablement (change in work)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a bilateral shoulder condition.  The worker claimed he began to experience shoulder discomfort when an additional task was added to his assembly job requiring overhead work.

DecKeywords: Cancer (lung); Evidence (testimony from other decision); Exposure (asbestos); Smoking
DecSummary: The worker's widow appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying dependency benefits for the worker's death from lung cancer in 1984.  The worker worked as a grinder in a foundry from 1950 to 1956.  He was a smoker.  The Board found that the worker did not have sufficient exposure to asbestos.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a right arm/shoulder condition.  The worker submitted that her condition was a disablement from the nature of her work on either of two days.  The Panel found that the worker's work on those days was not strenuous.  Medical reports did not relate the worker's condition to her work.  The appeal was dismissed.  [6 pages]

DecKeywords: Accident (occurrence); Delay (claim); Medical report (clinical notes); Medical report (early reports preferred)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a left knee injury which the worker claimed she suffered at work in February 1986.

DecKeywords: Second Injury and Enhancement Fund {SIEF} (preexisting condition); Transfer of costs
DecSummary: In December 1985 the worker fell and injured his right shoulder.  His employer, Employer 1, sought 100% SIEF relief for that disability, or alternatively, to have the costs of that accident transferred to Employer 2.

DecKeywords: Adjournment (Board submissions); Board Directives and Guidelines (chronic pain) (marked life disruption); Chronic pain (marked life disruption)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for chronic pain.  The Panel had seemingly conflicting statements from the Board regarding the requirement of establishing marked life disruption for entitlement now that the new Rating Schedule for chronic pain is being applied.

The worker suffered low back strains in 1973 and 1981.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement in 1988 and 1989.  On the evidence, the 1973 and 1981 injuries resolved shortly after the accidents.  The worker's condition in 1988 and 1989 was not related to the compensable accidents.  The appeal was dismissed.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Penalties; Board Directives and Guidelines (penalty assessments) (distortions); Board Directives and Guidelines (penalty assessments) (improved record)
DecSummary: The employer appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer confirming a penalty assessment for the years 1983-85.  The employer submitted that the assessment should be cancelled on the basis of distortions and improved safety record.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a neck, upper back, right shoulder, right forearm and right wrist condition.  The worker operated a spindle winding machine.  She submitted that her condition was either a chance event or a disablement.

The worker suffered a shoulder injury in 1979 when he was struck by a frame and received benefits for one week.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for his shoulder condition in 1985.

The worker sustained a compensable back injury in 1972 while attempting to lift a 200 pound weight by himself.  The worker received hospital treatment at the time, but he returned to work in January 1973 and thereafter performed various jobs which appeared to involve physical capacity.  He did not receive further medical treatment until 1986.  The worker suffered two accidents after 1972.  Following a 1981 accident involving his back, he received chiropractic treatment.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for right shoulder pain which began on January 17, 1988.  The worker worked as a packer, constructing large packing boxes.  From January 12 to January 15, 1988, the worker drove a forklift truck.  He submitted that his shoulder condition was related to his work driving the forklift.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (final decision of Board); Withdrawal (of appeal)
DecSummary: The employer was appealing a decision of the Hearings Officer denying the employer relief from costs of the worker's claim.  At the hearing, the employer requested that the Panel consider the appeal on the basis that benefits were paid to the worker improperly.  The Panel found that this issue had not been considered by the Hearings Officer.  The employer did not want to pursue the issue of SIEF relief.  The appeal was considered withdrawn.  [7 pages]

The worker suffered a knee injury in September 1986. Initially, he received temporary total disability benefits until April 1987. Subsequent decisions of the Board resulted in termination of benefits in November 1986. However, the Board decided not to recover the overpayment. The worker received a 5% pension retroactive to April 1987. The worker appealed denial of temporary total disability benefits from November 1986 to May 1987.

The worker suffered back injuries in July 1980 and May 1982.  He received benefits for about one month after each accident.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying further entitlement from August 1984 to October 1984.

The worker suffered a compensable injury for which he was awarded a pension.  He received a supplement from May 1986 to January 1989.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying a supplement from January 1989 to July 1989.

The worker's request to reconsider Decision No. 219/91 was denied.  In Decision No. 219/91, the hearing panel denied reimbursement for travel expenses from St. Catharines, where the worker now lived, to Brampton, where he used to live, for two doctor's appointments.  The hearing panel found that there was little treatment being offered.  The appointments were for supportive reassurance only, which could have been provided by a doctor in St. Catharines.
The worker suffered a low back injury for which he was awarded a 15% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying an increase in the pension.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer, except for specific sentences from a number of reports which were not relevant.  [4 pages]

DecKeywords: Continuity (of treatment); Disablement (strenuous work); Postal workers (letter carrier)
DecSummary: A letter carrier suffered compensable neck and shoulder problems in June 1975.  In September 1975, he was transferred to a lighter business delivery route.  In 1985, he returned to a heavier residential route.  He stopped work in October 1987 due to shoulder and upper back problems.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement to benefits in 1987.

DecKeywords: Pensions (assessment) (back); Temporary partial disability (level of benefits)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a low back injury in 1976.  The Hearings Officer increased the worker's pension from 30% to 60% and increased temporary benefits in 1989 and 1990 from 50% to 75%.  The employer appealed.

DecKeywords: Availability for employment (relocation); Available employment; Continuing entitlement; Procedure (absent parties)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a compensable injury in April 1987.  He received temporary total disability benefits until November 1987 and full temporary partial disability benefits from November 1987 until July 1988.  The employer appealed granting of benefits subsequent to June 1987.

Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.  [3 pages]
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer, except for one sentence which was not relevant.  [3 pages]

DecKeywords: Re-employment (notice from Board) (effective date); Re-employment (obligation to re-employ) (bankruptcy); Re-employment (obligation to re-employ) (commencement)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Reinstatement Officer finding that the employer had fulfilled its re-employment obligations.  The worker injured his back in May 1990.  He returned to work in June 1990.  One week later, he was given a separation slip.  In December 1990, the employer filed an assignment in bankruptcy.  In January 1991, the Board gave the employer a notice of fitness that the worker was capable of performing the essential duties of his job as of June 1990.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement.  Due to mechanical problems with a shunt truck which the worker was driving, a co-worker bumped him into the garage with another truck.

The worker suffered a neck and shoulder injury in 1983 and received benefits until December 1984.  Later, he was awarded a 10% pension for chronic pain retroactive to March 1986.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits from December 1984 to March 1986.

DecKeywords: Procedure (reconsideration) (constitution of Panel); Reconsideration (consideration of evidence)
DecSummary: The worker's request to reconsider Decision No. 754/91 was denied.  The request was considered by the original hearing panel on the recommendation of a different panel which felt that the nature of the request warranted comment by the original panel.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer granting 50% benefits from February 1986 to December 1986.  The Board granted full benefits subsequent to that date.  On the evidence, the Panel found that modified work offered by the employer was not suitable.  Due to the nature of the disability, it was difficult for the worker to find work on her own.  However, she did make some effort to look for work.  She was available for rehabilitation or work.  She was not disqualified from receiving full benefits.

The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for a shoulder disability which the worker claimed resulted from an accident at work.  The Panel found the worker to be a credible witness.  In addition, there was corroboration of the worker's testimony from two former co-workers.  The appeal was allowed.  [5 pages]

DecKeywords: Investigation by Tribunal; Jurisdiction, Tribunal (final decision of Board); Medical opinion (viral infection); Viral infection
DecSummary: In 1985 the worker began working as a health care assistant responsible for one particular child.  In October 1986 she began complaining of fatigue, headaches, confusion, lethargy, impaired memory and concentration, poor balance, and motor clumsiness.  The condition persisted through 1987.  The worker's doctor diagnosed a viral infection.  The worker's claim for benefits, on the basis that she contracted the illness through contact with the child, was denied by the Board.

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (substantial new evidence) (medical report)
DecSummary: The worker applied for leave to appeal a decision of the Appeal Board denying continuing entitlement for facial nerve damage.  The worker submitted new medical reports concerning neck and shoulder pain and spasms in his hands.

The worker injured her back at work in January 1986.  She returned to modified work in February 1986 and from that time until April 1989, she performed light work half of the time and was on general layoff the rest of the time.  During this period the worker made no claim for benefits while on general layoff and received no medical treatment, other than chiropractic treatment in April 1986. The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying benefits subsequent to March 1988.  The Hearings Officer found that a low back condition was not compensable.  On the evidence, the Panel found that worker aggravated preexisting asymptomatic spondylolisthesis in the accident.  The low back condition was also compensable.  The appeal was allowed.  [8 pages]

The worker suffered compensable injuries for which he was awarded a 10% pension.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying temporary benefits subsequent to February 1988. The worker was appealing the denial of continuing entitlement for a neck and shoulder disability.  At the proceedings before the Hearings Officer, the worker's claim to benefits for a psychotraumatic disability had been withdrawn.  When the Panel asked about the status of the claim for emotional disability, it was advised by the worker's representative that there was no emotional disability resulting from the accident and that it was the worker's intention only to pursue benefits for an organic condition.

The worker got a sliver in his left index finger in 1960.  The wound became infected and the infection, diagnosed as herpes simplex, has recurred on many occasions.  The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying an increase in the worker's 1% pension.

The worker was not entitled to ongoing compensation for a back disability subsequent to October 1986.  His soft tissue injury, which had resulted from a compensable accident in October 1980, had healed by February 1982.  The worker operated an auto body repair business from 1982 to October 1986. The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying an increase in his pension.

The respondents were not satisfied that the affidavit unequivocally established these facts.

DecSummary: A 71 year old retired worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying commutation of his pension.  The worker was receiving a 5% pension for knee disability and a 10% pension for shoulder disability.  The worker wanted a commutation of the 5% pension for use as he sees fit, perhaps to buy a cemetery plot.  The worker's income exceeded expenses by about $1,000 per month.  In addition, his spouse had monthly income of about $1,000.

The application of the worker's widow to reconsider Decision No. 127/91 was denied. New medical evidence raised no more than a possibility of a relationship between the worker's workplace exposure and his lung condition.

The application of the worker's widow to reconsider Decisions No. 212/91, 212/91R and 212/91R2, regarding entitlement to dependency benefits, was denied. The widow has made numerous applications to reconsider. The preponderance of evidence indicated that the worker's fatal heart attack was not related to his compensable lung condition.
